annotations.text:
Phosphor terminal.
Amber is the instrument: chrome, carets, your own numbers.
Cyan means you got it right, and is used for nothing else.
Red means you did not.
Parchment is content.

Syntax colour stays inside the amber family on purpose - a real CRT
never had a rainbow, and the typing surface must stay calm.

The Drill artboard shows the exact states the engine produces:
typed-correct lit at full brightness, the missed character marked in
red where it was expected, the caret sitting past it because forgiving
mode never stalls you, and everything still to come dimmed out.

The two leading dots are ghosted indentation - shown, never typed.
